chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the maximum duration of pregnancy in the mother's womb, how long is it? For the people say that perhaps it remains in her womb for two years. He said, 'They are lying. The furthest limit of pregnancy is nine months; it does not exceed a moment. If it increased by an hour, it would kill its mother before it exits.'
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration of pregnancy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the maximum gestation period as nine months, refuting the prevalent notion of a two-year duration by linking any excess to maternal mortality. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for determining the variable gestation period (ikhtilaf al-haml) used in calculating the waiting period (iddah) for widows and divorcees. The emphasis on the physiological limit underscores the precision of prophetic knowledge regarding human biology and its direct impact on legal rulings.
